acts.title: Boot Camp
acts.blurb: New hire on Foreman Brix's demolition crew. Learn to cut wires without lighting the fuse.

acts.title: Calling Cards
acts.blurb: Devices start turning up around town, each signed with a brass clock key.

acts.title: The Clock Tower
acts.blurb: The Clockmaker's last works. One tower, one fuse, no second chances.

twists.how: In engine.js newGame, right after G.dial is set from the mission, apply G.dial = Math.max(1, G.dial - param), so the fuse starts param steps shorter.
In engine.js newGame, right after setupEquip(M), move the last param cards of G.eq back to the front of G.eqPool (never below 0 cards), so fewer equipment cards are on the board.
When building newGame options, pass o.lv with the last computer seat set to 'easy' and every other computer seat at the chapter's setup.level, so one teammate is a rookie.
In engine.js infoSetup, skip the later('infoStd', ...) step for computer seats (SP(seat).human false) so only human seats place an opening info token; other info modes are untouched.

intro.text: Welcome to the crew, rookie. Today we only practise on blue wires, one to six.
Name a number, point at a teammate's wire. If it matches, you both cut. Simple.
Miss, and the fuse burns one step. I'll keep count. Try not to make me count high.

outro.text: Not one scorch mark. Same time tomorrow, and bring coffee.

opponent.name: The Training Rig
opponent.personality: A plywood practice board. Patient, predictable and very forgiving.

goal.text: Clear Job 1 (Boot Camp I): cut every wire before the fuse burns down.

stars.text: Make a solo cut at least once

easier.text: A smaller crew of sharper hands: just you and one steady teammate.

intro.text: New colour today. Every yellow wire counts as the same value: just 'yellow'.
There are only two of them in the rig. Find their owners before you name yellow.

outro.text: Two yellows, two clean cuts. I wrote that down twice for luck.

opponent.name: The Training Rig
opponent.personality: Now with two yellow wires hidden in the blues.

goal.text: Clear Job 2 (Boot Camp II): cut every wire, including both yellows.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: Work as a pair with your steadiest teammate.

intro.text: One red wire sits in this rig. Point at it and the whole job goes up. No second try.
Good news: the shelf has equipment now. Each card is a one-time trick for the crew.
If you're unsure, use a tool or ask a teammate's wire you're sure of.

outro.text: You walked right past the red. Steady hands, rookie.

opponent.name: The Training Rig
opponent.personality: Hides a single red wire among forty blues. Still patient, now dangerous.

goal.text: Clear Job 3 (Boot Camp III) without ever pointing at the red wire.

easier.text: Work as a pair with your steadiest teammate.

intro.text: Final exam: the full rig. All twelve blue values, a red and a yellow, maybe more.
The '?' markers show where a red or yellow MIGHT be. Not all of them are real.
Pass this and you get a crew jacket. Fail and you get a broom.

outro.text: That's a crew jacket. Wear it with pride.
Odd thing in the post today: a brass clock key and a card. 'See you soon.'

opponent.name: The Graduation Rig
opponent.personality: The full practice rig with decoy markers. Stern examiner, fair marker.
opponent.taunt: Rig wins this round. Reset the board and read the markers again.
opponent.praise: Every wire safe. Welcome to the crew, properly this time.

goal.text: Clear Job 8 (Graduation): all 48 blues plus the red and yellow candidates.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: Bring a fourth crewmate: the fuse starts one step longer.

intro.text: Call from the old cinema. A device, and a brass clock key taped to it.
One of the blue numbers is painted red, little crew. Guess which. Or rather, don't.
The card on the job sheet shows the painted number. Treat those four like reds.

outro.text: Paint doesn't fool us. Who signs their work 'the Clockmaker' anyway?

opponent.name: Vesper Quill, the Clockmaker
opponent.personality: A showman who builds puzzles, not just bombs. Polite, smug, loves a riddle.

goal.text: Clear Job 11 (Colourblind): never cut one of the four painted wires early.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: A tighter pair: two stands each, fewer surprises.

intro.text: I've had a quiet word with one of your crew. Their tokens will all be lies.
Whoever was dealt the foreman's card is the fibber. Their tokens mean 'NOT this'.
A lie you can read is as good as the truth. Read it backwards.

outro.text: Every lie told us where the truth wasn't. Thanks, Clockmaker.
Charming. Now let's see how you do when you don't know who is lying.

opponent.name: Vesper Quill, the Clockmaker
opponent.personality: Turns the crew's trust into a weapon. Enjoys watching you second-guess.

goal.text: Clear Job 17 (Fibber): read the fibber's false tokens as 'not this value'.

easier.text: Just you and one teammate: only one stand of lies to read.

intro.text: Somewhere on your crew is my weak link. Secret rule, secret face. Find them.
Character cards are dealt face down. Whoever got the foreman's card must obey a hidden rule.
Watch who cuts what. Accuse only when you're sure. And someone swiped one of our tools.

outro.text: Mask off. Turns out the weak link was just following a note in their lunchbox.
The note had an address: the old clock tower. Of course it did.

opponent.name: The Weak Link
opponent.personality: A crewmate under the Clockmaker's spell. Quiet, helpful-looking, bound by a secret rule.
opponent.taunt: You trusted the wrong hands. The Clockmaker sends his regards.
opponent.praise: Caught. I'm sorry, foreman. He said it was only a game.

twist.text: Boss rule: one fewer equipment card is on the board this job.

goal.text: Clear Job 34 (Mole Hunt): defuse the device while the weak link hides among you.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: Full equipment shelf and a fourth crewmate: the fuse starts one step longer.

intro.text: Welcome to my tower. The ground floor is a gift: no red wires at all.
Catch: all four 7s must be cut last, and all at once. Leave them for the end.
Clear everything else first. Then whoever holds only 7s takes the shot.

outro.text: Seven o'clock, and the floor is clear. Up the stairs, crew.

opponent.name: Vesper Quill, the Clockmaker
opponent.personality: Obsessed with the hour of seven. Generous on the surface, strict about order.

goal.text: Clear Job 46 (Lucky Sevens): cut every other wire, then all four 7s together.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: A pair of steady hands instead of a full crew.

intro.text: On this floor each of you holds one wire backwards. Only your friends can see it.
You must cut your own flipped wire yourself, no tools. Get it wrong and it's over.
Listen to our tokens before you touch the flipped one. We'll talk you through it.

outro.text: Blind cut, perfect cut. One floor left.
Impressive. The top floor is where I keep my masterpiece.

opponent.name: Vesper Quill, the Clockmaker
opponent.personality: Takes away what you can see and makes you trust what you can't.

goal.text: Clear Job 56 (Haywire): everyone cuts their own flipped wire without a miss.

easier.text: A pair of steady hands: fewer flipped wires to talk through.

intro.text: My masterpiece: twelve numbers, twelve rules. Each wire you finish wakes a new rule.
If the rule blocks you, say so and pass. If the whole crew is blocked for a round, boom.
And I've trimmed your fuse. Can't have you dawdling in my tower.
Four of us, one tower. Let's send him a calling card of our own.

outro.text: The tower is quiet. The Clockmaker's keys go in the evidence bag.
Final count: zero bombs left in town. Best number I've ever written.

opponent.name: Vesper Quill, the Clockmaker
opponent.personality: At his most theatrical. Every finished value changes the rules under your feet.
opponent.taunt: Tick, tock, boom. Come back when you can keep time, little crew.
opponent.praise: My masterpiece, undone by a demolition crew. I suppose that is a kind of art.

twist.text: Boss rule: the Clockmaker trimmed the fuse, it starts 1 step shorter.

goal.text: Clear Job 57 (Self-Destruct) with a fuse 1 step shorter than usual.

stars.text: Finish with 2 or more fuse steps left

easier.text: The full-length fuse and a tight pair of steady hands.
